documents.title: Follow-up Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Rebooked after the December cancellation (snow job, he said).
S: No new complaints. Drinking daily, unchanged. Thiamine on and off. Penicillin: stopped again. Denies swelling, bleeding, confusion, fevers.
O: vitals as charted. No jaundice, no ascites, mild tremor, no asterixis.
A/P: compensated alcoholic cirrhosis with chronic hep C; severe AUD; asplenia. Labs drawn. Brief intervention again, he can say back the risks but isn't changing. Penicillin re-sent with a pill box from the nurse. RTC 3-4 months.

documents.title: Lab Results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Labs stable from fall. No changes. Called, left message with results.

procedures.procedure: Telehealth visit, established patient, low MDM

documents.title: Video Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Video from his truck after work, connection poor at times. Identity confirmed with DOB.
Still working, crews kept going through the shutdown. No cough, no fever. Drinking the same or a bit more with the evenings at home. No belly swelling, no yellow eyes, no black stools.
No vitals today.
Plan: continue thiamine. Labs deferred until he can come in. Reviewed fever plan with asplenia: any temp over 101 means call right away, day or night. In-person in late summer.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Follow-up Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
S: First in-person since February. Missed August video. Things are tense at home, he and his wife 'aren't doing great.' Drinking more, he thinks. Appetite poor, mostly eats on the job site. No fevers, no bleeding, no swelling.
PHQ-2 2, says he's stressed rather than down.
O: vitals as charted, weight down a little. No jaundice, no ascites. Tremor.
A/P:
- AUD severe, worse with stress at home. AUDIT-C 12. Offered counseling referral and a program, declined. Continue thiamine.
- Cirrhosis compensated, hep C: labs.
- Asplenia: flu shot today. Not taking penicillin.
- Colon screening: turns 45 next month, will start with FIT in the spring.
RTC 4-5 months.

documents.title: Lab Results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Liver tests a little higher than spring, otherwise stable. Platelets in the 140s. Reviewed with pt by phone; he knows the drinking drives it.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Follow-up Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
S: He and his wife are divorcing, he moved into a rental in Florence in January. Says it's 'for the best' but he is drinking more since, most nights more than a bottle. Working. No fevers, no swelling, no bleeding, no confusion. COVID vaccine: plans to get it at the pharmacy next month.
O: weight 65 kg, down 2 kg from when he joined. No jaundice, no ascites, tremor.
A/P:
1. AUD severe, heavier with the divorce. Offered counseling, a program, and to talk about a medicine for cravings; he wants to 'handle it himself.' Door left open.
2. Cirrhosis, hep C: labs today.
3. Asplenia: same counseling. Penicillin on list, not taking.
4. Weight: eat with protein daily, thiamine.
5. FIT kit next visit.
RTC 2-3 months.

documents.title: Lab Results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Labs: same pattern, AST above ALT, albumin holding. Platelets lower this time at 96; recheck next visit. Portal message sent.

orders.reason: Blistering lesions on backs of hands after sun

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
S: For a few months now, blisters on the backs of both hands and up onto the forearms. They hurt, show up after a day in the sun or if he knocks his hand on something, and take weeks to heal. Thinks it's from work gloves or chemicals at the grounds job. No new soaps. No mouth sores. No joint pain.
Still drinking heavily since the divorce.
O: dorsal hands with a few crusted erosions and two intact tense blisters, scattered pink scars and darker patches. Forearms similar but milder. Rest of the skin clear.
A/P:
1. Blistering eruption on sun-exposed hands. With hep C and heavy drinking I worry about a porphyria picture. Referring to dermatology for evaluation. Gloves and long sleeves outdoors, sunscreen on the backs of the hands.
2. AUD severe: same discussion.
3. Colorectal screening: FIT kit given with instructions.
RTC after derm.

documents.title: FIT Result
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: FIT negative. Repeat in a couple of years. Portal message sent.

medications.sig: Take 1 tablet by mouth twice weekly
medications.reason: Porphyria cutanea tarda; patient has not started it

documents.title: Dermatology Consultation
documents.author: dermatology
documents.body:
OUTSIDE DERMATOLOGY GROUP - CONSULTATION
Date of service: 07/12/2021
Re: Gregory Kearney, DOB 11/11/1975
Referred by: primary care physician

Thank you for sending Mr. Kearney. He is a 45-year-old man with several months of painful blisters on the dorsal hands and forearms. New lesions come up after sun exposure or small bumps, heal slowly over weeks, and leave fragile skin with darker marks. He works outdoors as a laborer and groundskeeper.

History: chronic hepatitis C, never treated; heavy daily alcohol use; splenectomy after a car accident about eight years ago.
Medications per patient: thiamine; penicillin VK, which he admits he does not take.
Allergies: NKDA.
Family history: father with alcohol-related cirrhosis; mother with type 2 diabetes; no known porphyria or blood cancers.

Exam: multiple vesicles and bullae over the dorsal hands and distal forearms with crusted erosions, atrophic scars, milia and patchy hyperpigmentation. Face and trunk spared. Abdomen: the liver edge is palpable about 2 cm below the right costal margin.

Labs today: AST 96, ALT 71. Ferritin 812 ng/mL. HCV RNA detected. Urine total porphyrins 1,460 mcg/g creatinine (elevated).

Impression: porphyria cutanea tarda, in the setting of hepatitis C, heavy alcohol use and iron overload by ferritin.

Plan:
- Low-dose hydroxychloroquine 200 mg twice weekly; prescription given.
- Strict sun protection: gloves, long sleeves, broad-spectrum sunscreen, no tanning.
- Stopping alcohol is essential to control this.
- His hepatitis C should be addressed through his primary care physician.
- Follow up here in about 6 months.

Allergies: NKDA.

Thank you for this referral.
Dermatology

documents.title: Patient Call
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Pt called asking whether we got the skin doctor's note. We have not. He says he saw them July 12, they said it's a liver-related skin condition and gave him a pill to take twice a week. He has not filled it yet, wanted to know if it's 'safe with his liver.' Told him we'd request the consult letter and the PCP will call once we have it. Records request sent to the dermatology office.

documents.title: Records Received
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Dermatology consultation from 7/12/2021 received by fax after second request. Scanned and routed to PCP.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Follow-up Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
S: Dermatology letter finally came in August, reviewed. He has porphyria cutanea tarda. He never filled the hydroxychloroquine. Hands a little better since he started wearing gloves at work, still gets new blisters.
Drinking the same, living alone now.
O: vitals as charted. Dorsal hands with healing erosions and scars, no infection.
A/P:
1. PCT per dermatology. Low-dose hydroxychloroquine is reasonable with his liver at that dose, told him so; he says he'll fill it. Sun protection. Stopping alcohol is the main lever.
2. AUD severe: declined referral again.
3. Cirrhosis, hep C: labs next visit.
4. Flu shot today.
RTC 3 months.

orders.reason: Macrocytic anemia with low white count

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
S: About six weeks of being wiped out, winded on a flight of stairs or carrying lumber, and his tongue is sore and burns with hot coffee. No chest pain. No black stools or blood. Eating poorly, drinking heavily.
O: pale. Tongue red and smooth. Heart regular, soft systolic murmur. Lungs clear. No ascites.
CBC today: hemoglobin just under 9 with MCV about 111 and a low white count.
A/P:
1. Macrocytic anemia, new, with symptoms. Alcohol and nutrition are the likely story but given the low white count and asplenia I'd like hematology to see him. Urgent referral placed. Return sooner if chest pain or worse breathlessness.
2. AUD severe, cirrhosis: unchanged.
